That 11% reduction isn't magic. It comes almost entirely from restoring federal funding for Cost-Sharing Reductions (CSRs) payments that were halted by Trump and the Republicans in 2017. 
When those payments stopped, insurers raised premiums (especially Silver plans) through silver loading, which drove up costs and federal subsidies. Reinstating CSR funding simply reverses that hike.
So yes, premiums might drop about 11% on average, but it's not a new innovation....it's undoing a policy decision that inflated prices in the first place.

The Lower Health Care Premiums for All Americans Act exposes Washington's hypocrisy. Democrats forced taxpayers to subsidize insurance giants while premiums soared 75% under their failed system. This bill finally cuts through the bloat by expanding association health plans for small businesses and enforcing PBM transparency—forcing middlemen to reveal their drug pricing schemes.
